requirements.evidence: Requirement 1: .env.example:2,9 set APP_NAME=PegaFila and APP_LOCALE=pt_BR (fallback stays en) and phpunit.xml:22-24 pin APP_NAME/APP_LOCALE/APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE. Requirement 2: config/mail.php:128-129 sets mail.markdown.theme=pegafila and resources/views/vendor/mail/html/themes/pegafila.css:241-242 styles .button-primary with #0f7490 (also a:31, h1:41). Requirement 3: lang/pt_BR.json:559 adds "Reset your password" and :804 adds "Verify your email address", using existing "Hello!", "Reset Password" and "Verify Email Address" entries. Requirement 4: routes/web.php:11-24 define the four guest password routes (password.email throttled at :16) and PasswordResetController.php:29-41 always flashes passwords.sent, :58-88 validates token/email/password (min 8, letters, mixedCase, numbers, confirmed), resets with Hash::make, rotates remember_token and fires PasswordReset, redirecting to /. Requirement 5: routes/web.php:26-28 define verification.verify with auth+signed+throttle, and VerifyEmailController.php:19-35 403s on id/hash mismatch and redirects to /.

conventions.evidence: Most conventions are followed: inline validation for the one-field store() action (PasswordResetController.php:31-33), docblocks on public methods, {{ }} escaping in both views, PHPUnit env pins, and CHANGELOG.md:13 updated. Deviations: update() validates three fields inline (PasswordResetController.php:60-67) where conventions call for a Form Request once rules go beyond one or two fields, and the whole change ships no tests although the project mandates test-first development.

security.evidence: Password routes are guarded by guest and password.email is throttled (routes/web.php:11-17); verification.verify uses auth, signed and throttle:6,1 (routes/web.php:26-28) and VerifyEmailController.php:19-23 checks the user id and sha1 e-mail hash before marking verified. All input is validated (PasswordResetController.php:31-33, 60-67), CSRF is present, output is escaped (reset-password.blade.php:10,13), and no mass assignment is introduced (forceFill for password at PasswordResetController.php:73-75; #[Fillable]/#[Hidden] unchanged on User.php:16-17).

tests.evidence: change.diff:1-661 contains no tests/ file and no test modifications at all (grep for tests/, Test.php and Pest finds nothing); only the phpunit.xml:22-24 environment pins relate to testing. None of the new routes, notifications, views or the verification 403 path has coverage.

simplicity.evidence: The change is generally lean, but PasswordResetController.php:35-38 performs a User::where lookup only to decide whether to call Password::sendResetLink, which already resolves the user and returns a status without disclosing existence, so the extra query/guard is redundant; User.php:21 additionally uses the MustVerifyEmail trait that the base Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User already applies. The theme file is a required copy of the default theme, not speculative code.

readability.evidence: Small, focused controller methods with docblocks (PasswordResetController.php:29-41, 58-88; VerifyEmailController.php:15-35), clear names and consistent Laravel style; the routes file (routes/web.php:11-28) reads top to bottom, and there is no dead code or debug output in the diff.

scope.evidence: Every changed file serves the task: .env.example, phpunit.xml, config/mail.php, the pegafila theme CSS, lang/pt_BR.json, PasswordResetController, VerifyEmailController, the two auth views, routes/web.php and the CHANGELOG entry. No login/registration/logout, /home, Livewire, Blade layout, JS/SCSS, Docker or UI translation files were added.

issues.explanation: The change adds five endpoints, two notifications and two views with zero Pest/PHPUnit tests, so the project's 'no production code without a test' rule and the feature-test requirement for UI controllers are unmet.
update() validates three fields inline, whereas the conventions ask for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.

store() performs a User lookup only to decide whether to call Password::sendResetLink, which already resolves the user and handles unknown addresses without revealing them, so the extra query and guard are redundant.
Illuminate\Foundation\Auth\User already applies the MustVerifyEmail trait, so implementing the contract is sufficient and the added trait use is redundant.

review.summary: The change implements the pt-BR password-reset and e-mail-verification flows with the pegafila markdown theme and #0f7490 brand color, the required routes/controllers/views, the two missing subject translations and the locale/name pins. The production code reads as correct and secure, but it ships no automated tests at all, which the project's test-first rules make a merge blocker, and there are minor convention/simplicity nits (inline validation for three fields, a redundant user lookup and a redundant MustVerifyEmail trait use).
